source_text: Ioannem apostolum, non mundum istum, id est, caelum et terram, et omnia quae in eo substantialiter sunt, qui mundus factus est a Patre per Filium, reprehendisse, cum diceret: Omnia quae in mundo sunt, concupiscentia carnis est, et concupiscentia oculorum, et ambitio saeculi; quae non est a Patre, sed ex mundo est concupiscentiam carnis dixerit a Patre non esse
pass_a_gloss: Ioannem apostle, not world that, it is, heaven and earth, and all-things which in to-that substantially are, who world made is from Patre through son, reprehendisse, when/with diceret: all-things which in in-the-world are, desire of-flesh is, and desire oculorum, and ambitio of-the-age; which not is from Patre, but from in-the-world is desire of-flesh dixerit from Patre not to-be.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae

pass_b_english: When the apostle John said, “Everything in the world is the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, and worldly ambition, which is not from the Father but from the world” (1 John 2:16), he was not condemning this world—that is, heaven and earth and all the things that substantially exist in it, the world made by the Father through the Son.
[The desire of the flesh that is not from the Father] should be understood as excess.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Linked from Julian's wording or a clear allusion in the excerpt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
